pr_body:
Up until this point `bazci` has trawled the `bazel-bin` and
`bazel-testlogs` directories to find output artifacts for staging, but
this is not what we should be doing, as in doing so we're likely to find
stale, out-of-date files that belong to old builds or test runs.

We fix this by instead checking the
[build event protocol log](https://bazel.build/remote/bep), which
contains all the information we need for staging test results and built
binaries.

Closes #86773.

Release justification: Non-production code changes
Release note: None

issue_context.title: bazci: can collect .xml files from prior benchmark runs
issue_context.body:
Example: https://teamcity.cockroachdb.com/buildConfiguration/Cockroach_UnitTests_BazelUnitTests/6208678?buildTab=overview&showRootCauses=false&expandBuildChangesSection=true&expandBuildDeploymentsSection=true&expandBuildTestsSection=true#%2Fbazel-testlogs%2Fpkg%2Fccl%2Fchangefeedccl%2Fchangefeedccl_test

I suspect that this build agent ran a benchmark build configuration before running the unit tests, and the `test.xml` files from that run were leftover in `bazel-testlogs`. Then the unit test run came and picked up on these old `test.xml` files, not realizing they were stale.

Epic CRDB-15060
comments: > I suspect that this build agent ran a benchmark build configuration before running the unit tests, and the `test.xml` files from that run were leftover in `bazel-testlogs`. Then the unit test run came and picked up on these old `test.xml` files, not realizing they were stale. > That's also my hypothesis. Screenshots below prove that. (Note the nanosecond duration of the highlighted benchmark; it would be physically impossible to have the exact same timing on two independent runs :)
We probably want to set `--cache_test_results=no` for both of these jobs.

> We probably want to set --cache_test_results=no for both of these jobs.

This may fix some of these cases but isn't a surefire thing. The "real" solution is going to be a bit more heavyweight but shouldn't be prohibitively costly. I should have a PR out within a couple hours.
